NO traducir identificadores, claves de objetos, ids de modalidad, nombres de archivo ni tags de código.
Conservar siglas técnicas e imagenológicas intactas (MRI, CT, PET, SPECT, fMRI, EEG, MEG, T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, ADC, BOLD, 3T, TR, TE, TI).

glossary.SPECT: SPECT (Tomografía por emisión de fotón único)
glossary.BOLD: BOLD (dependiente del nivel de oxigenación sanguínea)

items.region.Frontal Pole.fn: Planning many steps ahead, weighing alternatives, and holding long-term goals.
items.region.Frontal Pole.clin: Damage blunts planning and initiative with little obvious deficit on routine exam.
items.region.Insular Cortex.fn: Interoception: feeling your own heartbeat, breathing, hunger, pain, taste and emotion.
items.region.Insular Cortex.clin: Infarcts can cause disordered taste, autonomic changes and loss of craving.
items.region.Superior Frontal Gyrus.fn: Self-awareness, working memory and, at its back end, the supplementary motor area.
items.region.Superior Frontal Gyrus.clin: Medial damage causes reduced spontaneous movement and speech (abulia).
items.region.Middle Frontal Gyrus.fn: Working memory and attention; its posterior part holds the frontal eye field that turns gaze.
items.region.Middle Frontal Gyrus.clin: Acute lesions make the eyes deviate toward the damaged side.
items.region.Inferior Frontal Gyrus pars trian: Part of Broca’s area (BA45): selecting words and meaning in speech.
items.region.Inferior Frontal Gyrus pars operc: Part of Broca’s area (BA44): planning the sequence of speech movements.
Left-sided damage: halting, effortful speech with preserved comprehension.
items.region.Subcallosal Cortex.fn: Mood regulation; area 25 under the corpus callosum.
items.region.Subcallosal Cortex.clin: A deep brain stimulation target for treatment-resistant depression.
items.region.Temporal Pole.fn: Linking faces, names and emotional memories (semantic hub).
items.region.Temporal Pole.clin: Atrophy in semantic dementia: words lose their meaning.
items.region.Superior Temporal Gyrus anterior: Auditory association cortex for sounds and speech.
items.region.Superior Temporal Gyrus posterior: Wernicke’s area on the left: understanding spoken language.
Left damage gives fluent but meaningless speech with poor comprehension.
items.region.Middle Temporal Gyrus posterior d: Linking words to meaning; near area MT for motion.
items.region.Middle Temporal Gyrus temporoocci: Bilateral damage causes akinetopsia (seeing motion as still frames).
items.region.Postcentral Gyrus.fn: Primary somatosensory cortex (S1): touch, pain, temperature and joint position, mapped as a homunculus.
items.region.Postcentral Gyrus.clin: Contralateral loss of fine sensation and position sense.
items.region.Superior Parietal Lobule.fn: Body map in space; guides reaching and eye–hand coordination.
items.region.Supramarginal Gyrus anterior divi: Integrating touch and body position; phonological working memory on the left.
Conduction aphasia (poor repetition) on the left.
items.region.Angular Gyrus.fn: Reading, writing, arithmetic and number sense on the left; bodily self-location on the right.
items.region.Angular Gyrus.clin: Gerstmann syndrome (left): agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia, left–right confusion.
items.region.Lateral Occipital Cortex superior: Visual association: spatial layout and motion.
items.region.Intracalcarine Cortex.fn: Primary visual cortex (V1) inside the calcarine sulcus.
items.region.Intracalcarine Cortex.clin: Contralateral homonymous hemianopia, often with macular sparing.
items.region.Frontal Medial Cortex.fn: Valuing choices, self-referential thought; a default-mode hub.
items.region.Supplementary Motor Area (juxtapo: Planning and initiating movement sequences, both sides.
Transient mutism and neglect of the opposite limbs after resection.
items.region.Paracingulate Gyrus.clin: Varies widely between people; subtle effects.
items.region.Cingulate Gyrus posterior divisio: Default-mode hub: memory retrieval and self-reflection.
Among the earliest areas affected in Alzheimer’s disease.
items.region.Precuneus.fn: Mental imagery, episodic memory and self-consciousness.
items.region.Precuneus.clin: Hypometabolic early in Alzheimer’s and in disorders of consciousness.
items.region.Cuneal Cortex.fn: Visual cortex above the calcarine sulcus: the lower visual field.
items.region.Parahippocampal Gyrus anterior di: Entorhinal cortex: the gateway into the hippocampus.
First area affected by tangles in Alzheimer’s disease.
items.region.Lingual Gyrus.fn: Visual cortex below the calcarine sulcus: the upper visual field and colour.
items.region.Temporal Fusiform Cortex posterio: Fusiform face area (especially on the right).
items.region.Temporal Occipital Fusiform Corte: Faces (right) and the visual word form area (left).
Pure alexia on the left; prosopagnosia on the right.
items.region.Frontal Operculum Cortex.clin: Speech output problems on the left.
items.region.Central Opercular Cortex.fn: Face, tongue and throat sensorimotor areas; swallowing.
items.region.Central Opercular Cortex.clin: Bilateral damage: Foix–Chavany–Marie syndrome (cannot move face voluntarily).
items.region.Parietal Operculum Cortex.fn: Secondary somatosensory cortex (S2): touch from both sides of the body, pain.
items.region.Planum Polare.fn: Auditory association cortex for melody and pitch.
items.region.Heschl's Gyrus (includes H1 and H: Primary auditory cortex (A1), arranged by sound frequency.
Unilateral damage is subtle; bilateral causes cortical deafness.
items.region.Planum Temporale.fn: Larger on the left; processes speech sounds and spatial hearing.
items.region.Supracalcarine Cortex.fn: Visual cortex just above the calcarine sulcus.
items.region.Occipital Pole.fn: Central (macular) vision; the largest piece of V1 per degree of visual field.
items.region.Lateral ventricle.fn: CSF-filled cavity; the choroid plexus inside produces about 500 mL of CSF a day.
items.region.Thalamus.fn: Relay and gate for almost all sensory input to the cortex, plus arousal and attention.
items.region.Thalamus.clin: Contralateral sensory loss; thalamic pain syndrome (Dejerine–Roussy).
items.region.Caudate.fn: Learning, habits and goal-directed action (basal ganglia).
items.region.Putamen.fn: Motor learning and movement selection (basal ganglia).
items.region.Globus pallidus.fn: Main output of the basal ganglia; iron-rich.
items.region.Globus pallidus.clin: GPi is a DBS target for dystonia and Parkinson’s disease.
items.region.Hippocampus.fn: Forming new long-term memories and mapping space.
items.region.Hippocampus.clin: Bilateral loss causes dense anterograde amnesia (patient H.M.).
items.region.Amygdala.fn: Detecting threat and tagging memories with emotion.
items.region.Nucleus accumbens.clin: DBS target studied for depression and addiction.
items.region.Brainstem.fn: Breathing, heart rate, consciousness (reticular formation), cranial nerves and every long tract.
items.region.Brainstem.clin: Small lesions cause crossed signs: cranial nerve palsy on one side, weakness on the other.
items.region.Cerebellar hemisphere.fn: Coordinating limb movement and timing, on the same side of the body.
items.region.Third ventricle.fn: Midline CSF cavity between the two thalami.
items.region.Third ventricle.clin: Colloid cysts here can block CSF flow suddenly.
items.region.Fourth ventricle.fn: CSF cavity between brainstem and cerebellum, draining to the subarachnoid space.
items.region.Fourth ventricle.clin: Posterior fossa tumours can obstruct it.
